svg.text: The PTX instruction shfl.sync in bfly (butterfly) mode:
partner = lane ^ offset (XOR, see 4), so lanes swap in pairs.
Why bfly: every lane needs the row max to rescale its own 16 scores.
down mode (partner = lane + offset) would leave it in lane 0 alone:

lane sends, here the maximum of its own 16 scores of the row. Every
lane sends its v and gets its partner's back, in one instruction.

svg.text: ^ is bitwise XOR, not a power. Write lane and offset in binary; each 1
bit of offset flips that bit of lane. offset=2 (0b10) flips bit 1,
Not 2 instead of 1: line 1 uses 2, line 2 uses 1. A quad's lanes 0–3
take 2 bits, and each line combines across one bit, so after both
every lane has all 4. Either order works.

svg.text: Quad 1 (lanes 4–7) works the same: 5 ^ 2 = 7, 6 ^ 1 = 7. Bits 2–4 of a lane say which
quad it is in, and never flip, so a partner is always in the same quad.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: Which lanes take part: one bit per lane, bit i for lane i. The other
cards follow quad 0 (lanes 0–3), but one shuffle runs the whole warp:
all 8 quads (lanes 0–31) swap at once, each on its own row. So the
mask covers 32 lanes. -1 in 32 bits is all ones, 0xFFFFFFFF (add 1 and
it wraps round to 0): every lane.
Why: a shuffle reads my partner's register, so my partner must run the
shuffle too. The mask lists the lanes that will, so the hardware knows
whom to wait for. In quad_reduce every lane runs it: all 32.

svg.text: One bit is one lane: 1 = 0b0001 lists lane 0 alone, not quad 0. Quad 0 takes four
bits, 0xF = 0b1111. Each hex digit is one quad, so 0x11111111 puts 0001 in every quad:
the first lane of each (0, 4, …, 28). 0xF731 builds a mask quad by quad: 1 = 0001
is written lane 31 … lane 0; the squares run lane 0 → 31. 0xFFFFFFFF read as an
unsigned number is 4294967295; as a signed 32-bit int it is -1, which is what the code
✗: all 32 lanes run the shuffle, but some are not listed, and lanes read unlisted
partners. The hardware promises nothing: v may come back as garbage.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: Walls between lanes. It cuts the 32 lanes into equal groups, and a
lane may read only from a partner in its own group. If the partner is
past a wall, the lane gets its own v back instead. Not the same as
mask (5): mask says which lanes run the shuffle.
The number holds two settings, the way 125 minutes is 2 hours and 5
minutes. Split it as big × 256 + small:
small: how far a lane may read inside its group. 31 means to the end.
big: sets the group size, 32 − big lanes (the hardware’s convention).

svg.text: One square per lane, lane 0 on the left; blue is quad 0. In the name, “mask” is
Why it changes nothing in quad_reduce
bfly’s partners, lane ^ 2 and lane ^ 1 (card 4), are always in the
same quad, so they never cross a wall, even with groups of 4. 31 is
also CuTe’s default; the code just spells it out.
down mode (card 2): partner = lane + 2. Quad 0 (lanes 0–3) works on
one row of S and quad 1 (lanes 4–7) on the next, so lanes 2 and 3
would read lanes 4 and 5: another row’s values.
What lanes 0–3 receive from line 1, under three settings:

svg.text: Each box: the value the lane receives (big) and the lane it came from (small).
Dashed: the partner was past a wall, so the lane got its own v back.
Both lines of quad_reduce on quad 0, for the maximum of row 0
Each lane starts with the maximum of its own 16 scores. Quads 1–7 do the same at the same time, on rows 1–7.
